title: Lateral hierarchy + sidebar fallback playbook
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a tactical playbook for a redesigned console navigation surface that treats the primary navigation as a lateral hierarchy with a deterministic sidebar fallback pattern. It documents wireframe intents, routing contracts, accessibility requirements, mobile and narrow-view behaviors, and a groomed backlog with acceptance criteria for engineering and PM.

Why this direction?
- Problem: current left-rail grows with features and creates deep vertical stacks that are hard to scan; deep links often land users on pages without clear task context.
- Goal: surface primary task families laterally (top-level horizontal clusters) while preserving a persistent contextual rail for task-specific actions. Provide a single, testable fallback: a compact, persistent sidebar that appears in tablet/desktop widths and collapses into a bottom-sheet action tray on small screens.
- Non-goal: this doc does not prescribe final visual styling or color tokens; it's focused on structure, routes, and operational behavior.

Design principles used:
1) Task-first: navigation groups map to customer mental models (e.g., Deployments, Models, Observability, Cost) not internal product areas.
2) Predictable fallback: exact behavior of the sidebar when space is constrained must be deterministic (not heuristics based on content height).
3) Shallow deep-links: every entity (model, deployment, route) has a single canonical route; the UI should mount the minimal context needed.
4) Stable focus: keyboard and screen reader focus must be preserved across route transitions when possible.
5) Measurable: every change must be observable via telemetry events listed below.

Proposed surface patterns (wireframe-level descriptions):
A) Lateral hierarchy (desktop / wide):
- Top horizontal cluster bar (H-bar) pinned beneath global header. H-bar contains 6–8 task clusters. Each cluster is a primary entrypoint (icon + short label). Hover or click opens a compact flyout with 3–6 sub-actions (no deep navigation inside flyouts).
- When a cluster is selected, the left rail converts into a contextual task rail showing entity-level navigation for that cluster (list of deployments/models/policies depending on context). The contextual rail is narrower (56–72px icons + collapsed labels) by default and can be expanded.
- Page scaffold: H-bar + contextual rail + content area (content area contains page header, breadcrumbs, action bar). Routing is controlled by top-level cluster + entity id + sub-route.

B) Sidebar fallback (tablet / constrained width):
- H-bar compresses to icons only. The contextual rail becomes a full-width left sidebar that can be toggled. The sidebar contains the same hierarchical content as the desktop contextual rail (expanded labels).
- The sidebar overlay has two modes: persistent (docked) and overlay (temporary). Default is docked for widths >= 900px. For mid-breakpoints use docked, for narrower use overlay.

C) Mobile (narrow):
- H-bar collapses into an icon row in the header; contextual navigation moves to a bottom-sheet (task tray) that slides up.
- Deep links open directly into content area; explicit action to open task tray via keyboard shortcut or header icon.

Routing semantics and canonical URL schema (wireframe contract):
- Base pattern: /console/:cluster/:entityType?/:entityId?/:subroute?
  - Examples:
    - /console/models/ -> models listing (cluster=models)
    - /console/models/model-123/config -> model config page (entity models, entityId=model-123, subroute=config)
    - /console/observability/alert-567/metrics -> observability->alert-567->metrics
- Route invariants:
  1) cluster segment is required and determines which H-bar cluster is visually active.
  2) entityType and entityId are optional; missing entityId means the listing or overview of that entity type.
  3) Subroutes are namespaced: config, logs, metrics, history, edit, run. Frontend must validate canonical forms and redirect non-canonical forms to canonical route (301-style client redirect).
- Redirect strategy: if user visits legacy routes (old left-rail paths), map to new canonical path and emit telemetry event nav.migration.redirected.

Accessibility and keyboard behavior:
- H-bar must be navigable by left/right arrow; clusters open using Enter/Space. Flyouts are focus-trapped while open.
- Contextual rail should be reachable via Ctrl+M (keyboard shortcut) and its first actionable item must be focused.
- When route changes programmatically (redirect or canonicalization), focus landing rules: if content header exists, move focus to h1; if not, to first form field or primary action.
- Screen reader labels: clusters must expose aria-current when active; flyout sub-actions use role=menu + aria-checked for toggle-type items.

Wireframe notes (developer-friendly):
- H-bar: 48px height, 16px horizontal padding per cluster, flyout max width 360px.
- Contextual rail: collapsed width 72px, expanded 264px.
- Content area: margin-left equals expanded rail width when rail docked; when overlay, content uses full width and sidebar overlays at z-index 800.

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Many clusters (>=9): enable an overflow chevron in H-bar that opens an ‘All tasks’ panel with search and keyboard jump-to.
- Extremely deep URL paths: max allowed subroute nesting = 1; deeper paths are flattened by canonicalization.
- Context loss on refresh: ensure client-side bootstrapping reads :cluster from URL and reprovisions contextual rail state before content render to avoid FOUC.

Backlog grooming (prioritized work items with acceptance criteria):
1) CONSOLE-IA-001: Implement H-bar component + flyout shell
   - Acceptance: H-bar renders clusters from feature flags; flyouts show sub-actions; keyboard nav passes unit tests; snapshot tests for DOM.
2) CONSOLE-IA-002: Contextual rail component with collapsed/expanded states
   - Acceptance: toggles animate within 120ms; persists state per user (local pref + server override); accessibility roles present.
3) CONSOLE-IA-003: Routing adapter & canonicalizer middleware
   - Acceptance: legacy routes redirect and emit nav.migration.redirected telemetry, new routes validate in router tests.
4) CONSOLE-IA-004: Sidebar overlay behavior for narrow widths + mobile bottom-sheet
   - Acceptance: bottom-sheet follows spec, drag to dismiss works on touch, opens via header icon.
5) CONSOLE-IA-005: Telemetry and metrics
   - Acceptance: events emitted: nav.cluster_selected, nav.flyout_open, nav.sidebar_toggled, nav.canonical_redirect; track conversion from deep-link to primary action within 15s.
6) CONSOLE-IA-006: Regression tests and visual QA checklist
   - Acceptance: cross-browser QA, visual diff tolerant thresholds, accessibility audit score >= 90 for primary flows.

Rollout plan (canary->gradual):
- Stage 1 (internal canary): behind feature flag for 5% internal users and 10% of beta orgs. Monitor nav.click-through-rate, time-to-action, and errors. Hold for 7 days.
- Stage 2 (org-level rollout): enable for orgs that opt-in via admin toggle. Collect qualitative feedback from Solutions Eng.
- Stage 3 (default enable): 50% of new sessions get new IA; full rollout at week+2 if key metrics stable.
- Rollback: global kill switch in control plane; per-org kill in console settings.

Telemetry and success metrics to watch:
- Time from landing to primary action (goal: reduce by 20% vs baseline).
- Deep-link failure rate (goal: <0.5%).
- Nav cluster click distribution and overflow usage.
- Accessibility regressions (automated A11y failures).

Loose open questions (for design + infra sync):
- Should H-bar clusters be user-configurable (reorder + pin)? (tradeoffs: additional prefs + complexity).
- How to represent multi-tenant orgs with many clusters? (overflow panel vs hierarchical grouping).
- Server-side persisted contextual rail state vs purely client-local settings (consistency vs sync complexity).

Immediate next steps (owners and short timeline):
- Week 0–1: Design produce final wireframes for H-bar flyouts and contextual rail (owner: Sofie).
- Week 1–2: Engineering scaffold components + router middleware (owner: Ivan).
- Week 2–3: Implement telemetry contracts and QA harness (owner: Marco).
- Week 3: Internal canary kickoff.

Appendix: shorthand sketches (text):
- Desktop: [Header]
  [H-bar: Models | Deployments | Observability | Cost | Integrations | Admin]
  [Contextual rail (collapsed) | Content area]
- Mobile: [Header (icons)] [Content] [Bottom-sheet task tray]

Notes-to-self: attach final interaction flows to JIRA stories and add example deep-link mappings for the migration script. Reach out to SRE about bootstrapping time for context state on cold loads.
